newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds stumble ahead of Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds stumble ahead of Greenspan.

text.p: *Australian bonds weaken markedly, reversing all the gains made on Monday, with the long end weakening most.
*Market waiting on Fed Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before a Senate Budget committee later today.
Australian bonds more than reversed the gains of Monday's unexpected rally as bonds sold off markedly after a quiet open.

With the U.S. open on Tuesday and ahead of the appearance of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan to testify on the economic outlook for 1997 before a U.S. Senate budget committee later on Tuesday, traders had expected a quiet day consolidating Monday's gains above support.
Instead, after a slow and slightly softer start, a bout of late morning selling saw the market fall through support, and it extended those losses through the afternoon.
"It's one of those cases of the market getting itself a little bit long," one trader said.
"I just think there's been a squaring up ahead of Greenspan speaking before the budget committee."

Long bonds, which had been the strongest performers on Monday, led the way lower on Tuesday. Previous resistance at 92.550 had been expected to prove solid support on the day, given the lack of offshore direction to the market and the optimism that next week's inflation data would be bond-friendly. Greenspan's testimony is expected to guide U.S. Treasury market sentiment ahead of the FOMC's February meeting.

Australian bond weakness sees curves close lower across the board, with widening in spreads to NZ exacerbated by rally in NZ market, and overnight strength in Canadian short end. Weth long end leading the way lower in price terms, futures curves steepens to back over 100 points.
